Here's a concise description of the video segment:

The video opens with a shot of a hand in a blue glove interacting with a bicycle at a bike sharing station. "NYC" in a white, outlined font is superimposed on the image. The perspective then shifts to a cyclist riding through city streets, with the words "BY" in the same style font overlaid on the screen. Continuing with the same style font, the video shows "BIKE" overlaid on the image of the bike on the street. The scene transitions to a street work crew of five men in hard hats and bright yellow vests repairing a section of the street. They are using various tools, including a jackhammer and a tamper machine. The camera quickly pans to show the cyclist speeding down the street, obscured by the blur of motion. Next, the video focuses on a man in orange reflective sunglasses looking directly into the camera, followed by a man in a blue shirt and backpack standing in a park with trees and benches. He is looking directly at the camera and smiling as he begins to speak.

The video segment begins with a street-level view of New York City, focusing on busy streets lined with tall buildings and billboards. The initial shot shows a row of vehicles, including a black truck with "Ram's Bottled Water & Cooler" written on the side, followed by a bright red tour bus. A man wearing a grey "BEST DAY EVER" t-shirt and a backpack then appears, riding a blue Citi Bike through Times Square, navigating through pedestrians and yellow cabs. The camera perspective shifts to first-person, showing the handlebars and the street ahead. A quick shot features pedestrians and bicyclists on a bridge, followed by a close-up of the man's leg pedaling the bike. His face appears again, this time wearing orange-tinted sunglasses. The shot transitions to an elevated view through a chain-link fence, overlooking heavy traffic on a city street. Finally, the video cuts to the man standing on a sidewalk, talking to another man in a blue collared shirt; text appears on screen labeling him as "CLARENCE ECKERSON JR. WWW.STREETFILMS.ORG". Overall, the segment transitions from general urban scenes to a personal view of a bicycle ride through various parts of New York City.

The video segment primarily features blue Citi Bike bicycles in New York City, with visuals including rows of parked bikes along the street, people using them, and information about the bikes. The first few shots display multiple parked Citi Bikes, highlighting their logo. As a man in shorts takes a bike from the rack, a text overlay says "There are 12,000 Citi Bikes all over NYC." and "60 Million Bike Trips have been taken since Citi Bike Launched in 2013”. The video then transitions to different street scenes in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, with people riding the Citi Bikes. The camera perspective alternates between street views and first-person point-of-view shots while riding the bike, providing a glimpse of the urban environment including a river, a ferry dock, and the Manhattan skyline. One man points to a street crossing and announces “That’s Christopher Walken,” pointing to a man walking up the stairs of a deli. In later scenes, a man on a Citi Bike rides along a bike lane blocked by trucks in the bicycle lane and describes that it is illegal. The video includes shots of people riding bikes over a bridge and scenes of street views featuring architectural buildings and other city elements.

Here's a detailed description of the video segment:

The video opens with a man in glasses, wearing a black jacket with "TCS New York City Marathon 2017" embroidered on it, standing on a walkway beside a bridge. He gestures and speaks about the creation of a dedicated lane for bicycles and pedestrians on the bridge. The camera then shows a woman riding a bicycle across the bridge behind the man. Following that, the camera focuses on a biker. Then, a transition occurs with a video of people cycling on the designated bike lane with the city skyline in the background. Two men on bicycles, one wearing a blue shirt and a backpack, the other wearing the same jacket as earlier, ride and converse as they pass the red bridge and enter Queens. The video shifts to views of cars on the highway and crosswalks. The man in the blue shirt mentions Queens reminds him of "Coming to America" and a snippet of the movie is shown, in which the characters dress in a stereotype of a New Yorker and one of them says: "I feel like a complete idiot". The man in the blue shirt looks for nature in Queens as he's riding a bike, and the video ends.

The video follows a man on a blue bicycle, riding through the streets and pathways of New York City, specifically focusing on a bike lane. He is wearing a blue polo shirt and shorts, with a helmet in the bike's front basket. Initially, he rides along a protected bike lane marked with bike symbols and arrows on the pavement. The surrounding scenery includes city streets, parked cars, and construction sites. The man expresses the importance of building infrastructure such as protected bike lanes before new residential developments, to avoid public resistance. He gestures with his hands while talking. Later, the video cuts to another man in orange sunglasses riding a bike in what appears to be a scenic park. The video transitions back to the first man, who is now riding along a pedestrian bridge with park benches and a cityscape view of the NYC skyline. The weather appears sunny with some clouds throughout the video. Later, the video shows the first man standing in front of the city landscape. In front of him is a green landscape, skyscrapers, and the ocean.  The text “POST NO BILLS” is on the green construction covering. There is also a road sign with the text “ROAD CLOSED LOCAL & EMERGENCY TRAFFIC ONLY.”

Here's a description of the video segment:

The video starts with a man in a blue shirt and glasses standing on a deck overlooking a grassy area with a view of the New York City skyline, explaining how the space is designed to absorb water as the sea levels rise. The scene transitions to show the grassy area along the riverfront, a walkway, and the city skyline in the background. Later, the view shifts to show a skyline with the Hudson River and the World Trade Center. The video then shifts again, this time showing a skyline with the East River and the Empire State Building. Next, the video shows what appears to be a park with the New York City skyline as a backdrop. Then, it transitions to footage of a man riding a blue Citi Bike, sharing the road with other bikers, construction workers, and, at one point, even having to maneuver around a work truck. One man who is biking with the man making the video states “What should I do there’s a truck in the bike lane? Do we hit him?” The footage shows signs for the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge and cyclists navigating the designated bike lanes. The man also states “this is quite a climb to go over this bridge, everything in New York is somewhat flat but, if you live in one of the boroughs you gotta go to Manhattan, you face a climb at some point”. The footage then includes a view of a busy street in Manhattan and a cyclist with a surfboard. Towards the end of the clip, the man on the bike says “Another good reason these [bike lanes] are so wide and also here you can see people that are in wheelchairs.”

The video opens with a view of the bike path in Central Park in New York City, where a jogger, cyclists, and a horse-drawn carriage travel along the road. Next, a man with glasses and a blue polo shirt appears, standing alongside the road, discussing how Central Park was made completely car-free last year after a long period of advocacy. As he speaks, the camera captures various scenes of Central Park including a horse-drawn carriage full of people and bicycles speeding along the road. Later, another man with orange glasses, standing along the bike path, expresses how relaxing Central Park is before pointing out the city buildings looming in the background. As the pair of cyclists leave the park, one man points out a Citi Bike that reads “Love & More”. Lastly, the scene changes to the city, where the cyclists ride down a city street before arriving at their destination.

The video begins with a close-up of yellow flowers attached to a pole, then pans out to reveal a white bicycle chained to the pole, decorated with flowers. The text on the sign reads: "CYCLIST KILLED HERE, REST IN PEACE, WWW.GHOSTBIKES.ORG" which is a memorial to cyclists who have died while riding their bikes. Then we see a man in bright orange sunglasses and a blue shirt standing on a sidewalk next to the memorial, discussing ghost bikes. As he stands on the sidewalk, another man wearing a blue shirt and an orange helmet rides by on a bike. The clip transitions to the view of the man wearing the orange helmet as he bikes with a young child in a child seat behind him on a bike path beside a traffic jam. The child, wearing a helmet and yellow shirt, looks directly at the camera. The clip transitions to two men near a brick building where one man waves at a window. An image of a toddler’s face is visible in the window. It transitions to the other man, the cyclist wearing the orange helmet, who gives a high-five to the same child, and then transitions to the toddler seated in a child-seat, looking forward. The cyclist wearing the orange helmet is now seen speaking to the toddler in the back child-seat as he explains that only bicycles can ride in the green lanes. The video transitions back to the cyclist wearing the orange helmet riding on the bike path in the sunshine with his toddler, who waves and smiles at the camera.
